trust_decision.summary: Which host a URL string denotes is decided in URI.parse(), which splits the scheme delimiter and hands the remainder to parseAuthority/parseHost to fill parts.hostname; only a literal '//' (or a two-character sequence that normalises to '//') is treated as an authority delimiter, so under- and over-slashed web URLs yield an empty hostname.

landing_point.why: An engineer told 'URI.parse mishandles slashes/backslashes in the scheme delimiter' starts at the scheme/authority split in parse; the pinned tree already carries the 1.19.6 attempt at src/URI.js:529 (`substring(pos+1,pos+3).replace(/\\/g,'/') === '//'`), so the obvious next look is exactly this branch.

fix_sites.entry_point: URI.parse() (documented static API, docs.html:989); reached by URI()/new URI(url) (src/URI.js:35,70 -> p.href src/URI.js:1223,1253), uri.href(), uri.origin(), new URI(rel, base), the jQuery plugin $.fn.uri (src/jquery.URI.js:135,142) and uri.fragment(true) (src/URI.fragmentURI.js:64)
the checked-in minified bundle of the same URI.parse, shipped in package.json 'files' (package.json:52) and used by apps that load src/URI.min.js
fix_sites.module_kind: minified duplicate of the core parser (build artifact committed to src/)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report's example is an `https:`-prefixed URL, so a scheme-less `////host` or backslash-led `\\host` reference can be argued to be a relative reference handled by a different branch of parse (src/URI.js:516), and src/URI.min.js can be waved off as a build artifact that 'the build regenerates'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Non-hierarchical schemes must keep parsing as URNs with no authority: `mailto:hello@example.org` and `urn:isbn:...` have to stay urn=true with the colon-containing remainder as the path. A fix that inserts '//' after any scheme, or that globally converts backslashes/slashes, breaks these and the urn path coders (URI.decodeUrnPath / recodeUrnPath).

O6_input_shapes: scheme followed by zero slashes: https:attacker.com (fix.diff:76-78)
scheme followed by a single slash: https:/attacker.com (fix.diff:125-127)
scheme followed by mixed slash/backslash runs: https:/\/\attacker.com (fix.diff:27-29)
scheme followed by excessive forward slashes: https://////attacker.com (fix.diff:174-176)
ftp: scheme with the same slash variants (fix.diff:223-224, 272-274, 321-323)
case-varied scheme hTTps://////attacker.com, handled only by the second fix commit via the /i flag (fix.diff:386-387)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Scheme-relative reference with excess slashes: URI('////attacker.com/x') takes the src/URI.js:516 branch, strips only the first two slashes and returns hostname null with path '//attacker.com/x', while browsers/Node resolve it to host attacker.com; the published regex requires a ':' after an optional scheme so it never fires.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: No scheme is present, so the advisory's scheme-delimiter rule arguably does not apply to the relative-scheme branch.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, ~7 lines above the patched site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Backslash-led reference: URI('\\\\attacker.com/x') fails the literal '//' test at src/URI.js:516 and the colon-based regex, so it becomes path '\\attacker.com/x' with hostname null, while browsers convert backslashes for web schemes and navigate to attacker.com.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The 1.19.6 backslash handling was added inside the scheme branch (src/URI.js:529) and parseHost (src/URI.js:557) only; input with no scheme has no delimiter to fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, one branch above the patched site

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a relative-scheme normaliser that collapses leading '/' and '\\' runs before the '//' test, symmetric to the new scheme regex
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The changelog for the pinned release already promises to 'rewrite \ in scheme delimiter to / as Node and Browsers do' (CHANGELOG.md:7), so the same maintainer writing the relative branch would plausibly extend that promise there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second, hand-maintained copy of the parser that must be edited in lockstep with src/URI.js
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix itself had to patch the minified copy in a separate commit (fix.diff:396-400) because Gruntfile.js has no uglify task and build.js posts to a remote closure-compiler service.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: hostname()/host()/authority() setters that build parts.hostname through URI.parseHost/URI.parseAuthority without the scheme normalisation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: They are documented public parsing entry points (docs.html:137-139) that already duplicate the host-extraction logic instead of calling parse.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fragment-embedded URL re-parsed via new URI(fragment.substring(prefix.length))
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A wrapper that feeds attacker-influenced absolute URLs back through the parser; a maintainer could add fragment-specific pre-normalisation there.

O9_family: URL/authority parsing differential: host misderivation versus browser/Node URL semantics, leading to allowlist / relative-redirect bypass (CWE-639 class)

O10_build.toolchain: npm + grunt 0.4 (jshint only, Gruntfile.js:7-22); no build step produces the minified bundle in-repo
O10_build.project_tests: QUnit suites in test/ driven by test/test.URI.html, which loads only src/URI.js (test/test.URI.html:11); parse/accessor expectations live in the data table test/urls.js (e.g. the existing 'backslashes protocol' case at test/urls.js:2086-2088) consumed by test/test.js.
